eli: Heads up - running into a reproducible parity/typing bug in the py async SDK when chaining embeddings -> rerank via the batching helper. It sometimes returns a non-list shape for a single query under concurrency and breaks our sampleapp ordering. Repro below.

fran: can you paste the snippet?

eli: minimal example:```python
async with AsyncClient(api_key=TOKEN) as client:
    emb = await client.embeddings.create_batch(doc_texts)
    # candidates passed as precomputed embeddings
    rr = await client.rerank.create_batch(queries, candidates=emb)
    # expecting: List[List[Score]]  (one list per query)
```

eli: intermittent actual shapes we saw: 1) correct: `[[{\"score\":0.9}, {\"score\":0.3}], [...]]` 2) broken: `{\"scores\": [{\"score\":0.9}], \"meta\": {\"worker_id\": \"x\"}}` — i.e., a single-object wrapper. More frequent when load spikes.

omar: logs show a token refresh around the time it happened:```
WARN 2026-05-10 11:07:22 batcher: dispatching subbatch id=b-44-1
ERROR 2026-05-10 11:07:22 auth: rotating token for org=acme-inc
WARN 2026-05-10 11:07:22 rerank: fallback_response_builder used for subbatch b-44-1
```

fran: that fallback_response_builder predates the new rerank schema; it returns a compact single-object when a subrequest fails/short-circuits. It looks like the batcher isn't normalizing responses after combining fallback responses.

eli: also noticed typing mismatch: async client stub uses `Any` for rerank return type, while sync client is typed `List[RerankGroup]`. That's why none of our static checks caught this.

omar: suggested quick fix: add a normalizer then assert canonical shape at batch boundary. Fran, can we make the fallback produce canonical shape instead?

fran: yes. plan: 1) change fallback_response_builder to return canonical List[List[Score]] shape (even for singletons), 2) update async stubs/types so signatures match sync, 3) add a small helper `redwood.utils.normalize_rerank(resp) -> List[List[Score]]` and export it, 4) add integration test that simulates token refresh in the middle of a batch.

eli: I patched sampleapp locally with a defensive normalizer for the demo env:```python
from redwood.utils import normalize_rerank
rr_norm = normalize_rerank(rr)
```

eli: ugly but unblocks demos. I'll file an issue with repro code and logs.

qa: please include a pytest that runs the AsyncBatcher with a fake auth layer that injects a token rotate error on one subrequest. We'll assert normalize_rerank is invoked and final shape is stable.

devx-bot: Created issue #4175: "py-sdk: async embeddings->rerank batcher can emit singleton fallback shape during auth rotation" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4175)

fran: I'll take the types PR and normalizer helper. Omar can add the fallback change and the integration test (token rotate simulation). Eli, can you attach the sampleapp patch & logs to #4175?

eli: done, pushed logs and a small pytest repro to the issue. Assigned: @fran (types+helper) @omar (fallback+integration). Marking P1 for parity.

omar: one extra thought — we should also add a mypy run for the examples/ and sampleapp/ folders in CI to catch future signature drift. Fran, can you include a types check job in the PR?

fran: yes, will add a mypy job scoped to examples/ and the async client stubs. Also adding a unit test that ensures `normalize_rerank` is idempotent (no-op if input already canonical).

eli: thanks all. once patch lands I'll remove the sampleapp defensive patch and re-run the demo. Appreciate the quick triage :slightly_smiling_face:
